mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds Rate above 5.25% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of expected corporate cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns over the 60-day window are not statistically lower than during the previous 60-day window with similar rate path (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in monthly employment growth (PAYEMS) accompanied by a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) signals a labor market strengthening that boosts investor confidence and drives S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases by at least 2% month-over-month while UNRATE decreases by at least 0.2 percentage points in the same or
failure_condition: The 20-day forward return is negative despite a statistically significant positive regression coefficient for the combined labor indicators (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) exceeding 0.5% for three consecutive months indicates accelerating demand growth, which elevates expected equity valuations and produces positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth rate > 0.5% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day ahead returns remain flat or negative despite the identified demand acceleration (Granger causality rejected at 5% significance).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) accompanied by a decline in consumer confidence proxies (not available in evidence - so omit interaction) suggests supply-side constraints that weigh on equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO decreases by at least 2% month-over-month for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than the prior 20-day window with similar INDPRO path (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 4%, the discount rate for future cash flows is expected to decline, supporting higher equity valuations and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
regime_hint: Fed Funds Rate normalization toward zero
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no significant improvement versus a 3-month pre-trigger baseline (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of declining labor turnover (PAYEMS < previous month for two months) suggests improved workforce stability, which reduces uncertainty and drives positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS decreases for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward return is negative despite a statistically significant negative lag in PAYEMS (p < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden one-time spike in retail sales (not available - so use GDPC1 as proxy for broad demand) followed by sustained growth above 2% monthly for 30 days indicates a demand rebound that elevates equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 monthly growth > 2% for 30 consecutive days after a > 1% one-time monthly increase
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than the 10-day pre-rebound window (p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the ratio of industrial production to capacity utilization (not directly available, so use INDPRO and HOUST interaction) falls below 0.7, it indicates underutilized capacity which suppresses growth expectations and produces negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO / HOUST ratio < 0.7 for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during a comparable period when the ratio was above 0.7 (p > 0.05).
